statement: Developer: Dr. Faranak "Fara" Kamangar MD, board-certified dermatologist, Department Chair, Palo Alto Medical Foundation.
Version: Not versioned; a learned language model based on dermatology knowledge from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles and texts, not a versioned software release.

Summary: DermGPT is a dermatology-focused AI chatbot, developed by a board-certified dermatologist, that allows dermatologists and staff to ask natural-language questions and receive cited answers drawn from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed dermatology articles and texts. It is intended as a practice-management and knowledge-access assistant rather than a stand-alone clinical decision maker.

Summary: DermGPT is a dermatology-focused AI chatbot, developed by a board-certified dermatologist, that allows dermatologists and staff to ask natural-language questions and receive cited answers drawn from more than 3,000 peer-reviewed dermatology articles and texts. It is intended as a practice-management and knowledge-access assistant rather than a stand-alone clinical decision maker.

Medical Purpose: Simplify everyday administrative tasks associated with dermatology practice management and improve access to dermatology knowledge, as an assistant rather than a stand-alone decision maker; does not replace medical care or clinical decision-making.

Acceptable Input: Natural-language prompts entered into the web chat app, e.g. questions about diagnoses, treatments, prior authorization letters, or differential diagnosis for a described presentation.

Output: Natural-language text answers with citations, drawn from a learned language model trained on more than 3,000 peer-reviewed dermatology articles and texts; outputs include text-based answers, patient handouts, and authorization letters.

Role in Decision-Making: A complementary tool rather than a sole decision-maker; the full underlying dataset is not fully disclosed, so healthcare professionals should continue independent clinical judgment to mitigate potential bias.

Intended Users: Dermatologists and dermatology practice staff (RNs, MAs, ancillary staff), as well as medical students, residents, and researchers. No specialized technical knowledge is required; preferred use is by medical professionals, though the developer notes users should proofread all AI-generated content for accuracy.

Known Performance Limitations: Not a substitute for professional medical advice; limited to its database of peer-reviewed publications; like all AI tools, lacks human creativity and intuition and is most effective when paired with a dermatology provider or staff who complement it with higher-level clinical judgment.

Required Clinician Oversight: No formal clinician oversight requirement, as this is an informational AI chatbot rather than a diagnostic device; standard risks apply, including potential for incorrect medical advice and bias if underlying literature is not inclusive. Users are advised to proofread all AI-generated content.

Performance: Developer-reported: in the developer's own practice, DermGPT saved approximately 30-60 minutes per day previously spent on EHR documentation, allowing clinic days to finish earlier; no independent, peer-reviewed performance studies identified.

Limitations in Evaluating Performance: The full training dataset is not fully disclosed, so it is unknown whether the peer-reviewed literature used is representative of the entire patient population; no independent validation has been published; reported time-savings are anecdotal/developer-reported.
Plans for Ongoing Monitoring: Continuously updated and improved by the developer, intended to remain current with new dermatology literature.
